Full enumeration of all 3^n words and an independent incremental suffix-only enumeration agree exactly at every length one through eight, producing counts 3,6,12,18,30,24,18,0. The complete eighteen-word maximum layer and its three symmetry orbits are regenerated from scratch.

originality.rationale: The primary paper proves that every ternary length-eight word contains some tangram and separately proves only that sufficiently long ternary words contain a tangram of cut number at most three. It does not state that length eight already suffices for the low-cut condition, nor enumerate the eighteen maximum avoiding words or their three symmetry classes. Targeted searches under direct and equivalent terminology found no covering finite census.
residual_risks: An unindexed computational note or private enumeration could contain the same sharp finite cutoff.

The source's sufficiently-long proof could potentially be tightened to eight by a short case analysis even though that cutoff is not stated; the complete eighteen-word equality layer remains a separate finite classification.
The result does not settle whether t(3) equals four or five.
